tagline: Marsh towns of the North Shore, from clipper yards to clams.
intro: This stretch of the North Shore road leaves Newburyport, laid out on the high south bank of the Merrimack where clipper ships were once built, and heads south past the Newbury marshes to Ipswich, Essex and Cape Ann. The whole byway runs some ninety miles and ties together fourteen coastal towns between Salisbury and Lynn.

Around Essex the low country is part of the Great Marsh, the salt marsh that shapes much of this coast. There the first settlers lived by farming, fishing and clamming, and most of all by building ships.

moments.title: Ipswich
moments.text: Incorporated in 1634, the town still has about 59 First Period houses standing and lived in, more than any other community in the country.

moments.title: Essex
moments.text: The town built schooners for Gloucester's fishing fleet until engines replaced sail, and in the summer of 1916 a clam shack owner here reportedly fried the first clam.

moments.title: Gloucester
moments.text: On the harbor stands the Man at the Wheel, the fishermen's memorial, dedicated to they that go down to the sea in ships.

sources.label: Essex Heritage, Essex Coastal Scenic Byway
